Generally speaking, shooting somebody is a felony; so is pointing a gun at them, or displaying a gun in an implied threat. Doing any of these things as a means of self-protection can work as an affirmative defense to what would otherwise be a felony charge.

Now here's the issue... while it varies from state to state, as a general rule you can only claim self-defense if you are faced with an immediate, viable threat of severe harm. In most states, if you are outside your house, you are expected to retreat whenever possible. If you chose to stand and fight, you surrender your claim of self-defense.

Brandishing presents two problems - the first is that it may give your opponent a valid claim of self defense. He can say something like, "we were arguing, then he pulled a gun, so I was in fear of my life and I pounded his head in with this rock". It looks a lot like you escalated a verbal disagreement into a potentially lethal physical fight. Unless you have some proof of your side of the story, things can get bad pretty quickly.

And before you respond with the obvious question, keep in mind that an affirmative defense places the burden of proof on you.

The second issue is that drawing a gun and not firing it is presumptive evidence that you had the time and space to retreat. In states where you are expected to retreat, you cannot claim self defense if this avenue was open to you.

Yes, the law is totally whacked, and yes, the burden of proof really is on you. So what's the right thing to do?

Retreat. Get out of Dodge.
